The taste, consistency, etc. of the sauce were all just right and it was just right so that it wasn't too sweet or ruined the taste of the pork cutlet itself. The pork cutlet didn't feel greasy at all as the oil was drained well. The radish radish kimchi served as a garnish was as good as any Korean restaurant, and the mayonnaise-based penne was also very standard. And while I was eating it, I remembered the schnitzel I used to eat in Austria. The freshness and thickness of the meat were both perfect, and it was an excellent meal that showed all the essence and basics of Korean-style king pork cutlet. I went to many places to find the taste of pho that I had in the US and Canada, but it was the most perfect. I regret not ordering the rice noodles separately, but I plan to try it on my next visit. reviews.text:
As Haebangchon became a tourist destination due to the revival of Sinheung Market, the prices of eating out in the neighborhood naturally rose significantly. You can easily find prices ranging from well over 10,000 won for a brunch meal to over 7,000 won for a cup of coffee. They say that hipness comes with responsibility, but the prices are bound to be disappointing for locals who have lived here for a long time.

Meanwhile, this store, casually located on the second floor of the road, is the home of the few remaining Haebangchon locals. A table was filled with people on a late Tuesday night, and when I entered the store, my aunt naturally asked, “Would you like to eat pork belly?” This is a set of green onion kimchi, bracken, bean sprouts, and bellflower sprouts that I think would be delicious when grilled with meat. It comes with fresh ssam vegetables and, no, a fried egg? With the price of 180g of raw pork belly at 14,000 won (it even went up not long ago), and soju and beer at 4,000 won, I wonder if this place was 10 years ago.

If you eat all the meat, be sure to get the ‘fried rice’, which is not on the menu and only locals know. All you have to do is cut the remaining meat, stir-fried kimchi, and vegetables into small pieces with scissors, store them, and then order ‘Gonggibap’. Then, a bowl of rice is served with sesame oil and dried seaweed powder, and you can stir-fry it yourself and eat it. Why is this space loved by locals? This place captures the atmosphere of Haebangchon before it became hip. I also fell in love.

When I ordered alcohol, they gave me several glasses to choose from, and it was already starting to win people's hearts. Even though the sizes of the glasses look similar, they are surprisingly different, so it is not easy to estimate the amount of alcohol to be consumed.
The banto served as an appetizer was topped with ricotta cheese, and it was more refreshing, fragrant, and sweet than I imagined. If it were on the menu, I would have ordered more. The assorted sashimi was well aged and brought out the savory flavor of the winter fish, and Buta Gakuni, which I had low expectations for, was chosen as the first pick by half of the group because the texture and taste of the chewy and soft mashed potatoes, arugula, and pork below would go so well together. Needless to say, the famous Mackerel Bon Sushi was soft, refreshing, and very delicious without any fishy taste. I remember being spoiled by bong sushi a few times, so I timidly ordered only 1 roll, but I was very disappointed. The sea bream mala goes well with the soft and light sea bream steak and the mild mala sauce, and the crunchy garnish that feels like a croissant breaks up the boring texture of the soft texture.
The Suji fish cake soup was just as expected, with a rich yet refreshing taste that went particularly well with pot rice. In addition to the bong sushi at this restaurant, we remember the pot rice that satisfied us so much. Even though I said, “Wow, I’m full,” I ate it all. The seasoning of the pot rice is amazing, goes well with the fried green onions, and above all, the texture of the rice is really good (I can't remember what kind of fish it is...the type of fish seems to change from time to time). Most of the group wanted to come just to eat pot rice. The most unpopular one was the shrimp mara. reviews.text:
I remember the first time I encountered Jjamppong in Gyo-dong, Gangneung a few years ago. I was impressed by the mussels that were prepared to be easy to eat, the pork that was sliced ​​into chunks, the seafood ingredients that did not disappear until the soup was completely drained, the light chives, and the unique spicy spicy flavor that went well with them. Jjamppong from Gyo-dong, which we thought would come back at some point, has now spread all over the country. Even in my neighborhood, which is on the outskirts of Incheon, there are more than three specialty stores selling Gyodong Jjamppong.

Meanwhile, I was curious about this store that had ‘Specializing in Gyodong Jjamppong’ on its sign. In Haebangchon, which is filled with the world's hip stores, it is giving off the vibe of a neighborhood Chinese restaurant without any care. During meal times, there is a line of people who look like local residents and the delivery phone line is buzzing. Another attraction is that the prices are cheap enough to make you forget about the cost of living in Haebangchon, which has risen as the world becomes more hip. Yes, I knew it when I saw myself scratching the floor. It's been a while since I found the taste of Gyodong.

reviews.author: FNH
reviews.text:
I visited on a weekend evening. I made a reservation in advance and reserved a bar table, but my husband liked the bar table and I didn't. The reason is that sitting at the bar table doesn't mean you can see the food being cooked, but you can only watch the cocktails being made, so it wasn't fun. I think you need to reserve the table next to the road (in the picture) in advance. We weren't able to sit down because we didn't mention it when making a reservation. They said they were already fully booked.

Interior: I think the interior is great. The lighting and atmosphere are great ~ romantic atmosphere. Ah, I'm not sure why, but unlike other restaurants, there were a lot of male customers. Even though I think about it, I'm not sure. Definitely not a place to visit with children. There are a lot of couples at the table, a lot of friends, a lot of company employees, and it seems to be perfect for business as well.

Food: Oh, I love it! Haha, first of all, it's delicious, it's reasonable, and the innovative design and taste ~ good ~ Ah, among them, I highly recommend the roti (we ate 3 plates of roti..) It's a taste that makes me keep ordering it. Normally, I don't remember much food the next day after going to a restaurant, but "Roti" comes to mind. I can't remember the names of all the dishes, but I really wanted to try them all. The price is reasonable, not burdensome, and the taste is good! Kudos! I’m curious about the chef’s face.

Wine: ㅠㅠ.. I’m disappointed about the wine. Compared to other restaurants, the staff seems to be well-educated about wine, but compared to the restaurant feel and interior service... the presentation is lacking (bringing and serving the wine when you choose it, showing it, checking if the wine you chose is right, asking the doctor, and opening). I think it's more appropriate for a satay restaurant if you do a fair amount of wine.

And what I regret is that there are almost no wines under 100,000 won. I think the price of wine can be very burdensome for some people. There aren't many under 100,000 won, there aren't many in the upper 100,000 won range, and the prices are rising significantly. Wine is more expensive than other similar restaurants. I think you can get a decent wine for around 150,000 won. Of course, everyone has different standards for wine.

Also, not to brag, but humbly, even though I tend to drink a bit of wine, there were some wines I wasn't familiar with, so the wine list was very interesting, but the wine list was too large for Korean standards. Rather, why not narrow down a wine list that matches the food and revise the reasonably priced wine menu a bit?

Service: I am satisfied with this part! Not like employees these days? Overall, everyone is friendly~

I 100% intend to visit again ~ Other than what I thought about the wine, the food was delicious and the atmosphere was nice! And I keep thinking about roti... ㅠㅠ!... This is a restaurant I think I can go back to in a few months.

Ah, to my lover, when I was doing business, I said, “I paid some attention and looked for it.” A place you can take to ~

reviews.author: clouds clouds
reviews.text:
📍Seoul Haebangchon/Itaewon Midnight Forest
-
Ragu Margherita (₩9,900)
Margherita pizza made with ragu sauce as the base. The part with the toppings is thin so you can really taste the ragu flavor, and the end part is thick, making it savory and chewy. Italian pizza needs a slightly burnt leg to be attractive. Margherita refers to a pizza that symbolizes the green, white, and red Italian flag with ingredients such as tomatoes, and raguso sauce refers to a thick sauce made by boiling minced meat and vegetables.
-
Prosciutto Bismarck (₩15,000)
A sweet and attractive pizza topped with prosciutto and a poached egg on top of an Italian pizza. Bismarck Pizza is a pizza where you put a poached egg on top of the pizza, pop it open, and eat it as a sauce. There is a story that it originated from Prussia's Chancellor Bismarck, who used to eat a soft-boiled fried egg on top of a steak. The combination of salty prosciutto and the sweet taste of the pizza base is delicious.
-
I recommend ordering cole slaw on the side. It's really delicious if you put it on pizza and wrap it in Italian ssambap style. It's a combination recommended by the boss. The sauce is thick and coats the noodles well, giving it a chewy texture and a delicious mushroom flavor. The mushroom cream congilli is also top-notch. The cream soaks into the pasta noodles and is delicious.
-
This is not an American pizza, but an Italian handmade pizza made by kneading the dough by hand. Midnight Forest, an Italian bistro run by a chef specializing in Western food. From the dough to the homemade pizza and homemade ragu sauce that is boiled for 4-5 hours every day, the taste is made with great care and at an affordable price. wonderland.
-
There are only a few pizzas in Korea with such delicious dough. They say they make it themselves and it's not too salty and the seasoning is just right. The prices are reasonable and the music is hip, so I think I'll go again. The forest-like interior is also very pretty and has a nice atmosphere. Delicious dough and cheese. The most important thing is that the toppings are rich and the cheese is soft and not tough even when cooled.
-

reviews.text:
“Simple is the best: Patty’s counterattack”

1. Even if you just go to McDonald's, you will have a moment of indecision due to the numerous burgers. Deciding which burger to eat can also be stressful for modern people. The name of this burger restaurant was created with the goal of relieving stress. This restaurant has only one menu. You only have to choose one, two or three patties.

2. Based on the success of Haebangchon, we opened a delivery restaurant in Gangnam, and I couldn't help but see the benefits, so I tried double and triple orders. The packaging appears to be quite half-hearted, but the burgers delivered are very hot due to the instant cooking and fast delivery, making this an impressive first experience.

3. The composition of the burger is very simple. Bun + patty + cheese + pickle is a very basic and primitive composition of a hamburger. The first burger at Louis Lunch in New Haven (the city where Yale University is located), famous for being the first restaurant to make hamburgers in the United States, consisted of a single beef patty between square pieces of bread. When I lived in the U.S., I remember buying hamburger patties from Costco, grilling them, and eating them with just ketchup between slices of bread. This combination of bread and patty can never be delicious unless the patty has both taste and texture. It is a primal taste that enjoys the balance of sweet carbohydrates with a meaty, salty and oily patty. Perhaps this can be said to be the taste of .

4. No Stress Burger pursues this original hamburger taste. A simple burger bun without any techniques is soft and adds sweetness to the burger. Although it is thin and slightly burnt, it contains just the right amount of beef fat, so when you layer it a few layers, the synergy between the flavor and juice is incredible. In addition, the patty space created between the missing oil and the chewy texture of the meat make it a very delicious patty. There are a few pickles that give it a slightly sour flavor as an accent.

5. Simple and delicious without stress. If you aren't confident in your patty, you can't make a burger like this. Of all the burgers I've had in Korea so far, I experienced the best patty in terms of meaty aroma, texture, and taste. The more patties here, the better. Doubles are better than singles... triples are better than doubles.



PS: Hamburgers are delicious, but buffalo wings are also really delicious. The taste is somewhat Korean... but it would have been better if the sauce was real ranch sauce... hehe.

PS2: Since the Gangnam branch is closed, I am reviewing the Yongsan branch.

reviews.text:
Growing up just 45 minutes from the Mexican border, eating good Mexican food was never a problem. So living in Korea was a mixed experience for Mexican food. I've had some of the worst Mexican food here, but I've also had some amazingly good Mexican food in Seoul. Today, I would like to introduce one of the best places.

Venditos doesn't claim to offer 100% authentic Mexican food, but describes itself as fusion Mexican, but I don't mind at all because the food is delicious! Some purists may balk at this statement, but honestly, if the food is done right, does it really matter if it's done right?
This restaurant is another project of the Manimal group, which includes Daeyoung Kim (DY) as one of its founders. If you've been to places like Manimal Smokehouse, Motor City, or Hunnit Deli, you already know their standards.

I've been to Benditos three times and tried a variety of dishes. Let's start with the basics. Good tortillas are essential to making good tacos, and the tortillas here are unique and unlike anything I've had before. I've tried a few different tacos here, but in my opinion, the brisket tacos are by far the best. The brisket and pulled pork are smoked at Manimal and brought here daily. Another highlight was the ‘Mexican Porchetta with Chicharrón’. As soon as I took a bite, I got a dopamine rush. It's true.

Drinks offer a variety of mezcals and tequilas, including a tequila sampler. The tequila menu is divided into Blanco, Reposado, Anejo, and Extra Anejo. Cocktails are also available. My favorite menu item is ‘Texas Jungle Juice (serves 2)’. It was a little disappointing that there was no Mexican beer. Other than Corona, they only have Stella Artois draft beer. I usually think that if the food is delicious, that's the most important thing, but I have to admit that drinking Stella with tacos feels a little off.

My only complaint is that some of the fries that come with the guacamole are vegan, which I personally am not a fan of. It was okay at first, but the more I ate it, the more I started to hate it. I think it would be better to eat more regular tortilla chips.

reviews.author: ethan ghymn
reviews.text:
I stopped by because I was curious about Billion Box, which I saw in Janghee's review a few days ago.

I've never tasted White Castle's original sliders in the U.S., so I can't compare, but I've seen them in a lot of videos from American mukbang YouTubers, and I was curious, so next time I get the chance, I wanted to stop by and try local hamburger franchises like White Castle and Whataburger instead of national hamburger franchises like McDonald's, Burger King, and Wendy's. I heard that Billion Box here is offering White Castle's copycat sliders, and the common handmade burger restaurants are only expensive and I don't know if the taste is particularly good. Even the prices here were cheap, so I thought this might be a store I might like.

The store was near the Seongdo Pharmacy intersection on Gyeongnidan-gil, and I remember passing by it before, but the store logo was similar to that of Supreme, a once-popular fashion brand, so I passed by without even knowing it was a hamburger store.

Even though it was around lunch time, there were no customers, so the clerks looked at their phones and said, “Welcome!” as I entered.

The store is decorated in white and red colors and has the feel of In-N-Out Burger. There is also an In-N-Out Burger paper bag on one side of the store, so it seems like the store has looked at and studied American hamburger stores in many ways.

When I looked at the menu before visiting, I thought the single combo came with two French fries, but when I looked at the blog, I saw that it was a set of two sliders, one French fries, and a drink.

In other words, the single combo was a set of two sliders with one patty, French fries, and a drink, and the double double combo had the same French fries and drinks, but changed into two sliders with two patties instead of one.

The double double combo seemed to be high in calories and I didn't know what it tasted like, so I decided to order the single combo and eat it.

When I was asked to choose a drink, I wondered if there was my favorite Dr. Pepper, but that wasn't the case. It was just the usual cola, diet cola, Sprite, and Fanta, so I chose cola.

The store has a bar table-type window with a ladder that can seat about 3 people, so I sit down and look around the store. There is a panel with a lot of White Castle Instagram photos on the window, and one of the photos includes a copycat of a White Castle slider, so it's definitely more like a Kagenga with White Castle as a motif.

Foreign customers also come in and order takeout, and the store smells like a faint oily smell, but it's very subtle so it doesn't bother me.

After waiting a bit, the single combo I ordered finally came out, and I was told that drink refills were available, so let me know if I needed anything.Blogs say that the size of the slider is small, but in reality, it is so small that it can be eaten in about four bites, so I understand why the combo menu includes two sliders as standard. It feels smaller than the simplest cheeseburger at McDonald's, but the bun is thicker.

Excited to see what it would taste like, I took the single slider out of the box and grabbed it. The bun was soft and when I pressed it with my hand, it almost felt like butter oozing out. But when I bit into it, the bun was so buttery that it almost felt as if it had been dipped in butter and baked with a buttery flavor and smell.

The patty has a slightly spicy and salty taste, so I feel like there are likes and dislikes, but I like the taste of American burgers because it is different from the burgers commonly found in Korea and I like the taste of salty American burgers. However, the patty is thin, so I will have to order a double double combo next time.

The finely chopped onions are good and the sauce feels like In-N-Out.

I asked the person who baked the sliders, who was probably the owner, if he was receiving delivery of the buns because they had a buttery flavor, and he said yes, and that the buns had a lot of butter in them and that they also added a lot of butter when baking them.

The price is cheap, but I asked if they use good quality meat, and they told me that they only use one part of 100% Australian beef.

I asked if they had tried the original sliders at White Castle and they said yes, but did they taste similar? When I asked him about it, he said that wasn't the case and explained that White Castle's method is to steam-cook the patties, but here, they are cooked in a regular pan and the taste is different, but the appearance is based on White Castle's sliders.

French fries feel like they're just common, but it's nice that they're not pre-fried like in the franchise.

I asked what the store's name, Billion Box, meant, and they said it just meant 1 trillion, with a box at the end. I don't know what it meant exactly, but it sounded like they wanted to become rich.

I like hamburgers in general, but when I go to so-called handmade burger places, except for a few places, I don't notice any differences, they don't feel original, the balance isn't good, and I've been disappointed because they're sloppy. I passed by this store before, but I didn't know it was a hamburger store. After reading Janghee's review, I was curious and looked for Billion Box's sliders, which are not the brioche buns that I like, which are not the brioche buns that I see so often these days, which feel worse when the overall balance is not right. Although they use a bun, the difference is clearly felt because the bun is fluffy and buttery. The patty is also salty, so it's different from a typical hamburger. It has an American feel to it, so it's fresh and good. The size of the slider is also small, so it's easy to eat, and it's a good experience because it has the original feel of this restaurant.
